note: private_message_notify is the Private Message submodule that emails thread members when a new message arrives, via the Message + Message Notify stack. Service private_message_notify.notifier (PrivateMessageNotifierInterface::notify($message,$thread)). Its shouldSend() reads private_message.settings keys (enable_notifications, notify_by_default, notify_when_using, number_of_seconds_considered_away) plus per-user user.data. The notification is a 'message' entity of template 'private_message_notification' (fields field_message_private_message, field_message_pm_thread) sent through message_notify.sender. hook_private_message_notify_exclude() lets modules exclude recipients. No routes/permissions/schema of its own; it drives the parent's config. This is a submodule glue over message_notify, so it uses 3 easy / 1 medium / 1 hard, grounded in the private_message.settings flags shouldSend() reads.

evals.prompt: In the Drupal private_message_notify submodule, what triggers an email notification when a new private message is posted, and which service/method does the work?
evals.expected_output: When a new message is added to a thread (hook_private_message_new_message), the private_message_notify.notifier service's notify($message, $thread) runs. It builds a 'message' entity of template private_message_notification and sends it through message_notify.sender to eligible thread members.

evals.prompt: Which private_message.settings flags decide whether private_message_notify actually sends a notification to a recipient?
evals.expected_output: shouldSend() sends only when private_message.settings:enable_notifications is TRUE, the recipient is eligible (their user.data 'receive_notification' is on, or unset while notify_by_default is TRUE), and either notify_when_using is 'yes' or the recipient has been away longer than number_of_seconds_considered_away. Per-user user.data overrides the system defaults.

evals.prompt: How can another module stop private_message_notify from emailing a particular recipient about a new message?
evals.expected_output: Implement hook_private_message_notify_exclude(PrivateMessageInterface $privateMessage, PrivateMessageThreadInterface $thread, array &$exclude): add the recipient's UID to the &$exclude array (e.g. based on a mute flag). getNotificationRecipients() drops those UIDs.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, inspect the Private Message configuration and state whether new users are notified of private messages by default (the notify-by-default setting that private_message_notify's shouldSend() consults).
evals.expected_output: notify-by-default is OFF: private_message.settings:notify_by_default is FALSE (shipped default is TRUE). So a user who has made no personal choice will NOT receive notifications. Read it with drush config:get private_message.settings notify_by_default.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, make private message email notifications work by default: turn notifications ON site-wide and make them apply to users who have not set a personal preference. Apply the change to the live configuration.
evals.expected_output: Set private_message.settings:enable_notifications to TRUE and notify_by_default to TRUE (e.g. drush config:set private_message.settings enable_notifications 1 -y; drush config:set private_message.settings notify_by_default 1 -y) - the two flags the notifier's shouldSend() requires to email by default. Verify checks both are TRUE.
